My land has grown wheat and corn since before I was born. My husband farmed this way, my father-in-law farmed this way. I am 67 now and my knees hurt, but I know this land and I know what it wants.

I have 6 mu in the village plots. I will plant winter wheat on all 6 mu in October, harvest in June, then immediately plant summer corn on the same 6 mu. This is what every family here does. The soil here in Quzhou is deep and flat — it is good for grain. I would not know what to do with vegetables or cotton.

For wheat, I will buy the improved variety seeds from the township seed station — the Jimai kind the extension people told us about years ago. For corn, I will buy hybrid seeds, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has. The hybrid corn gives more grain and I need the yield. I can't carry heavier sacks than I used to, but I still need the money.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer and urea before seeding, then spread more urea in spring when the wheat joints. My son helps me carry the bags. For corn, I spread compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea when it reaches my waist.

Water is the worry here. The well water is getting deeper every year. For wheat I will water three times — before the ground freezes, at jointing, and at heading. For corn the summer rains usually come, but I will irrigate once if it is dry at tasseling.

I spray herbicide in spring on the wheat, and again when the corn is young. If I see rust or aphids on the wheat I will call my son and we will spray again.

I use rotary tillage before wheat planting — I hire the village tractor man. For corn I plant straight into the wheat stubble, no plowing. That saves money and the soil stays better.
